messages:
ajohnson: hitting intermittent production crashes for a customer using JSON mode streaming. app sees "invalid JSON" errors and downstream processors fail. only happens at high qps, ~99p. stack: 

ajohnson: python service log: 
```
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 256 (char 255)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/json/decoder.py", line 344, in raw_decode
    obj, end = self.scan_once(s, idx)
```

marta: can you share repro steps and SDK versions? is this python-only? :eyes:

ajohnson: repro is flaky but consistent under load. SDKs: python 0.9.2, ts 1.3.0, go 0.7.1. using streaming with json-mode and heartbeat enabled. payloads are structured outputs (objects with nested arrays).

ajohnson: quick repro steps:
1) open streaming completion with json mode
2) send long array in the structured field (~2k chars) and frequently cancel/reauth flows
3) consumer parses ndjson by splitting on newlines

ajohnson: sample captured stream (note fragmentation between chunks):
```
{"id":1,"out":{"items":["hello","worl
```
```
d","more"]}}
```

marta: that split looks like a newline missing between frames — consumer splitting on "\n" will break if server-side framing emits partial objects. do you see the same bytes on the wire in tcpdump?

ken: observed similar from Go clients. go json decoder errors look like: 
```
invalid character '\x00' looking for beginning of value
```
- often at the same percentile as the python failures.

sara: I believe this surfaced after a change to streaming chunk composition + proxy gzip passthrough in the infra last week. proxy sometimes emits chunked bodies in mid-utf8 codepoint. could be our chunking + ndjson assumptions colliding.

ajohnson: attaching a tiny repro harness I ran locally (python):
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
it = client.stream.generate(..., mode='json')
for chunk in it:
    # naive split-on-newline consumer
    buffer += chunk
    while '\n' in buffer:
        line, buffer = buffer.split('\n',1)
        parse_json(line)
```

ajohnson: when the SDK yields a partial object (no trailing newline) parse_json throws. sometimes heartbeat frames are inserted, sometimes not.

marta: short-term mitigation: treat stream consumers as framing-agnostic — buffer until a valid JSON object is parsed or add a sentinel newline after each object server-side. also we've got an internal patch for the python sdk to coalesce partial frames before yielding.

marta: workaround details: upgrade python sdk to 0.9.3 which contains a streaming coalescer; for TS/Go we have PRs in review that add the same behavior.

ken: adding my minimal go parser change we tested: keep a persistent buffer and attempt json.Unmarshal progressively instead of strict 
strings.Split on 
. reduced failures from ~2% -> 0.02% in stress.

ken: sample stress result: 10k streams, failures: 205 -> 2 when switching parser.

ci-bot: deploy id: deploy-cc723f3 applied to staging at 1967895400. linked ticket: INF-4321.

marta: next steps:
- eng-runtime to confirm server-side chunk boundaries (marta -> assignee: @ken).
- eng-ml to validate heartbeat frame semantics (sara).
- SDKs: merge coalescing patches and ship 0.9.3 (python), 1.3.1 (ts), 0.7.2 (go).

ajohnson: customer is asking for ETA. can we get a hotfix release for python today?

marta: yes, will cut python 0.9.3 hotfix today and ping support when published. will also include a short README note on streaming framing best practices for consumers. :white_check_mark:

ken: created a tiny repro repo and upload link to internal artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/repro/jsonmode-frag.tar.gz

ajohnson: cool. thanks — please include the sample ndjson capture I pasted so CS can forward to customer.

sara: marking infra change for rollback if this continues after patches.

ajohnson: :thumbsup: will stand by for hotfix and STATUS update.
